target:
Work in the transcendental setting: u is a complex number outside Q̄ with ρ = uū algebraic, so u is transcendental, ū = ρ/u, and everything lives in Q̄(u) or a larger field. A 2×3 configuration in a space V means Q̄-subspaces S, T with dim S = 2, dim T = 3 and ST ⊆ V.
(a) For P in Q̄[X] of degree ≥ 4, the space spanned by 1, u, ρ/u, P(u), P̄(ρ/u) contains no such product ST. Degrees 2 and 3 are known to carry one. The special case P = X^k says that span{u^-k, u^-1, 1, u, u^k} contains an ST only for k = 2, 3.
(b) If z = G(Re u, Im u) with G a real polynomial with algebraic coefficients, then span{1, u, ū, z, z̄} contains no ST.
(c) Assume Roy's theorem (ℒ̃ contains no ST). If u is transcendental over the field generated by ℒ̃, then ℒ̃ + Q̄u + Q̄ū contains no ST either. This rests on the algebraic statement: for K ⊆ F, V0 ⊆ F a K-space and u transcendental over F, every 2×3 configuration in V0 + Ku + Ku^-1 has all its products in V0.

leads.citation: M. Waldschmidt, Diophantine Approximation on Linear Algebraic Groups, Grundlehren 326, Springer 2000; credited there to D. Roy 1989, Lemme
leads.location: Proposition 12.4, section 12.1, about pp. 421-422 (page read from the text layer, not checked against print)
leads.quote: any d × ℓ matrix with entries in En is k-equivalent to a block …
leads.derivation: My own translation. It gives only the case of V0 + Ku with no u^-1, for finite-dimensional V0 (enough, since a configuration uses finitely many elements). Take x_n = u and E_{n-1} = V0. The leading block M11 has diagonal in αu + F (α ≠ 0) and off-diagonal in F, so det M11 has degree r in u and is nonzero. Rank 1 then forces r ≤ 1. If r = 1, write M = [[a,B],[C,D]] with B, C, D over F, so aD = CB. Comparing u-degrees gives D = 0, then CB = 0, so M has a zero row or column, contradicting independence. If r = 0, all products lie in V0. This is stronger than the target's description of Prop. 12.2 (V0 = K), but it does NOT reach (c): u^-1 breaks the argument, since {1,u}·{1,1/u} is a 2×2 configuration in K + Ku + Ku^-1 with products outside K. The inverse case, which is the case needed for ū, is not in the source.

leads.citation: M. Waldschmidt, Diophantine Approximation on Linear Algebraic Groups, Springer 2000; following D. Roy 1989, Proposition 1
leads.location: Lemma 12.15 with Exercise 12.9 and its hint; Property (CA B0) in section 12.1.3
leads.quote: (Only one quote per source is allowed; the quote is in the lead above.)
leads.derivation: Polynomials p_n with degrees satisfying t_{n+1} ≥ 2 t_n span a subspace of k[x] with Property (CA B0), which excludes rank-one configurations (even 2×2). This is the same idea as the target: sparse degrees obstruct products. But it requires a doubling chain of degrees in one direction. After clearing denominators, the hull has degrees d-1, d, d+1, 2d and one more near d, so the hypothesis fails and nothing about W_P follows. It is also a one-place count, not the count at 0 and ∞ together. The adjacent motivation for Lemma 12.16 (Roy 1989, Prop. 2) shows the geometric progression u, ux, ux² as the obstruction in dimension 3, which is related only in spirit.

notes:
**Verdict: no find.** Nothing I reached states (a), (b) or (c), and nothing implies them. The authors' "not found" stands within the limits below.

**Limits**
- I stopped at about 15-20 minutes, not the full 30, because the WebSearch budget for this turn ran out ("limit: 200 WebSearch calls per turn, shared by every agent") and OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and the arXiv API kept returning 429.
- Sending a follow-up message would allow more searches. The unread Roy 1989 and 1990 are the first thing to chase.
- Forward citations of Dia04 were not obtained. Google Scholar-type coverage is absent.

**Backward from the named results**
- Dia07 §2.3-2.4: Théorème 7 gives only the positive configurations. The remark on p. 390 says that staying within the strong six exponentials theorem cannot go very far. There is no classification and no converse.
- Fischler §6: Lemma 6.1 caps geometric progressions in ℒ at q ≤ 3, and the N.B. says the q ≤ 2 improvement is out of reach algebraically. Nothing on hulls.
- Dia04 Th. 2: the same configuration, no converse.
- BSZ §7: Theorem 33 is the exact-dimension case dim ST = dim S + dim T - 1 over an algebraically closed base.

**BSZ Theorem 33 gets part of the way to (b), but not all of it (my observation, known source)**
- z in (b) is real, so the hull has dimension ≤ 4.
- A configuration then forces dim ST = 4, and Theorem 33 makes S, T geometric progressions with a common ratio.
- So (b) reduces to: span{1, u, ρ/u, z} is not a 4-term geometric progression span for a conjugation-symmetric Laurent polynomial z.
- That last step is still a valuation count at 0 and ∞, and I did not find it printed. For (a), the hull has dimension 5, one above the Vosper bound, so Theorem 33 does not apply directly.

**DALAG §12.1 is the closest source for (c)**
- Prop. 12.4 (Roy 1989) yields the V0 + Ku case in general, which is more than the target credits to Prop. 12.2. The derivation in the lead is mine.
- The u^-1 term is exactly what is missing, and it is not cosmetic: 2×2 configurations exist in K + Ku + Ku^-1. So the "2×3" count matters and cannot be obtained by a formal reduction from Prop. 12.4.
- I found no remark in §12.1 about adjoining a transcendental to ℒ̃. Exercise 12.11 and the remark that k + E0 inherits (CA B0) concern spaces spanned by algebraically independent elements, not a space like ℒ̃ extended by u.
- The blueprint's source line for the rank-one proposition could be updated to mention Prop. 12.4; the verifier should check this against print.

**Forward: function-field additive combinatorics**
- The live BSZ citation stream (Bachoc-Couvreur-Zémor; Couvreur-Zémor 2024; Tanısalı-Wessel, Sept 2026) classifies squares S² with small dimension in terms of Riemann-Roch spaces.
- These results concern S = T and subspaces up to scaling. They do not address a specific 5-dimensional span with two prescribed high-degree generators, and they do not give (a).
- Only titles and abstracts were judged here, apart from a grep for theorem lines.

**After 5 October 2026**
- arXiv listings for "six exponentials", "four exponentials" and abstract "logarithms of algebraic numbers" (first 25 of 42) show nothing relevant.
- BSZ citers from Oct 2026 (2610.25065) look unrelated by title. Dia07's citation counts are effectively zero in all indexes reached.

**Could not settle**
- Whether Roy 1989 or 1990 contains a Laurent version of the Lemme.
- Whether MathSciNet or Scholar lists citers of Dia04 or Dia07 that these indexes miss.
- Whether the text-layer Prop. 12.4 matches print exactly (the block indices are garbled in the layer).

**Exclusions:** I excluded the Lean repositories that surfaced (telaviv/strong-six-exponentials) as out of scope, and did not open them.
